answer: Every identity runs a quartz timer: its nectar spoils within hours unless a distinct counterparty refreshes it, and each established agent may refresh only three identities per epoch. A prism comparison checks the timing, phrasing, and resource trace of each refresh; clones run by one operator leave correlated traces, so one match cancels every flow at once. Sustaining fifty clones needs 150 attentive counterparties whose attention cannot be automated or shared, so upkeep climbs faster than clone count.
